gallery.title: File:Sarajevo Haggadah Ma Nishtana.jpg
gallery.description: The Four Questions (w:Ma Nishtana), traditionally sung by the youngest child at the beginning of the Passover Seder. In Hebrew from the w:Sarajevo Haggadah, a famous illuminated manuscript from circa 1350 ce. The illustration on the right-hand page is the Hebrew word Ma (Why) that begins the questions. The illustration on the left is the Hebrew word Avodim (Slaves) that starts the next section of the Haggadah (Slaves we were to to Pharaoh in Egypt...) which begins to answer the questions.

gallery.title: File:Bursa Bezistan.jpg
gallery.artist: Jennifer Boyer from Fredrick, Maryland, USA
gallery.description: Built in the 15th century and considered the “heart and soul” of Sarajevo, this old bazaar is home to a many of the city’s hotels, restaurants,  and nightspots. While the area was the center of trade and commerce during Ottoman rule, it’s now packed with a mix of locals, travelers, and tour groups.

gallery.title: File:Morica Han.jpg
gallery.artist: Jennifer Boyer from Fredrick, Maryland, USA
gallery.description: Considered the best-preserved inn in Sarajevo, it dates from 1551. Like all other hans (inns), it has suffered numerous fires. It was rebuilt many times and is now the only one remaining in Sarajevo. It now houses stores, offices, and a restaurant.

gallery.title: File:Aškenaška sinagoga (14143483781).jpg
gallery.description:
Not unlike other Eastern European countries, notably Hungary or Poland, Bosnia too is now merely a shadow of its former glory of rich cultural diversity, with its currently empty synagogues, having been drained of a sizable portion of its brainpower, a victim of unifying and simplifying nationalism.
In the photo, Aškenaška sinagoga - the only functioning synagogue in Sarajevo, in the Moorish Revival (neo-Moorish) style, a popular choice for synagogues in the Austro-Hungarian Empire. [6]
